questions.question: Define gravity and mass, and explain why we notice the Earth's gravity but not the pull between two people.
questions.expected_answer: Gravity is a non-contact force of attraction between any two objects that have mass. Mass is the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms. Gravity is a very weak force; the pull between two people is extremely small because their masses are small, but the Earth has an enormous mass, so its pull on us is strong enough to notice as weight.

questions.question: Explain how mass and distance affect the force of gravity, and the difference between mass and weight using a 45 kg learner on the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: The greater the masses, the stronger the gravity; the greater the distance, the weaker the gravity (doubling distance makes it four times weaker). Mass is the amount of matter and stays the same everywhere; weight is the force of gravity on the mass, measured in newtons, and changes with location. The learner's mass is 45 kg on Earth and the Moon, but on the Moon, whose gravity is about one sixth of Earth's (less mass), their weight is about one sixth of their Earth weight.

questions.question: Explain how gravity holds the Moon in orbit around the Earth, using a model.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon moves sideways very fast; without gravity it would travel in a straight line into space. Earth's gravity pulls it towards the Earth; together, sideways motion and gravity bend its path into a curved orbit, so it is always falling towards the Earth but missing. Model: swing a stopper on a string in a circle; the string's pull (like gravity) keeps it moving in a circle; if released, the stopper flies off in a straight line.
